headline: Bank Indonesia Faces Pressure to Hike Rates as MSCI Warning Weakens Rupiah
summary: Bank Indonesia faces growing pressure to raise interest rates after a threat from MSCI to cut the country's market status triggered a stock rout and weakened the rupiah.
why: Emerging market central banks must defend their local currencies and manage capital flows when external index providers threaten reclassifications that spark capital outflows.

impacts.name: Indonesia
impacts.why: Index reclassification threats and a weakening rupiah put severe pressure on local financial markets and monetary policy.

why_moved: The rupiah and local stocks declined following MSCI's warning of potential standalone status, prompting expectations of defensive central bank intervention.
